nodes.label: Ladder over pairs (worse than scalar ladder)
nodes.norm_label: ladder over pairs (worse than scalar ladder)
nodes.rationale: Best pair ladder (4,4,5,6) 2.7542 bits vs scalar 2.7089 with 25x larger table: spreading over 421 pairs flattens the distribution so power-of-two rungs no longer follow it. Vector coding inflates tables, the one thing the ladder exists to avoid.

nodes.label: Mutual information between neighbouring exponents (<= 0.010 bits)
nodes.norm_label: mutual information between neighbouring exponents (<= 0.010 bits)
nodes.rationale: Six windows spread across the model to avoid embedding-matrix bias; max I(X;Y)=0.00998 bits, order-1 context model +0.0000 bits/symbol: no correlation to exploit, so vector coding can only recover code redundancy.

nodes.label: Phase 1: CPU validation
nodes.rationale: Entropy 2.645 bits, Huffman 32.48% bit-exact, ladder (1,1,1,2) 31.62% (-0.86 pts) with 43 distinct symbols; the ladder shape chosen on synthetic Gaussian data transfers to real data.

nodes.label: Phase 2b: access-pattern optimisation
nodes.rationale: Output staging 1.92x, input 1.01x, both 1.48x (worse) on Pascal; at BLOCK=256 input staging 4.38x confirms L2 story. Huffman/ladder redone: Huffman BLOCK=64/128thr/output 4.80 ms vs ladder 5.07.

nodes.label: Phase 2d: cross-field mutual information
nodes.rationale: Exact 65,536-bin histogram over all unique weights: H(sign,exp,mant)=10.578 true floor, I(exp;mant)=0.040 concentrated in binades 122-123; field split achieves 10.678 vs 10.602 full alphabet: 0.076 bits/weight given away.

nodes.label: Approaching Shannon Bound with Lossless LLM Weight Compression (arXiv 2606.15789, ISCA 2026)
nodes.norm_label: approaching shannon bound with lossless llm weight compression (arxiv 2606.15789, isca 2026)
nodes.rationale: Current frontier: rANS over the whole 16-bit symbol fused into the GEMM, up to 11x DFloat11 throughput. Dominates this design on rate by construction (0.076 bits/weight bounded on Qwen3-0.6B); its speed comes from fusion, not the coder.

nodes.label: DFloat11 (arXiv 2504.11651, NeurIPS 2025)
nodes.rationale: Direct reference: Huffman over BF16 exponents, ~30% reduction. Its decode.cu uses fixed 8 bytes per thread with 5-bit gaps (~0.21 bits/weight index), a two-pass decode with block prefix-sum, output merged to BF16 through shared memory, LUTs in global via __ldg. Not a drop-in comparison for the 8-bit index.

nodes.label: Schwartz & Kallick 1964: Generating a canonical prefix encoding
nodes.norm_label: schwartz & kallick 1964: generating a canonical prefix encoding

nodes.label: 8-bit block index + warp prefix-sum
nodes.rationale: Block lengths have little spread (130-273 bits at BLOCK=64) so a uint8 length delta per block plus one uint32 per 32-block superblock (1.125 B/block vs 4) suffices; offset recovered with 5 __shfl_up_sync steps. +2.25 points at zero measurable cost; removes the reason to want large BLOCK. Only reaches BLOCK=128.

nodes.label: Fixed symbols / fixed bits / fixed both trilemma
nodes.norm_label: fixed symbols / fixed bits / fixed both trilemma
nodes.rationale: Fixed symbols per block needs an index (this repo); fixed bits per block gives O(1) addressing but unknown weights per block (DFloat11); fixed both is a fixed-rate lossy code (BC/ASTC). Losslessness closes the third corner so the index is unavoidable.

nodes.label: Canonical Huffman over BF16 exponents
nodes.rationale: Incumbent entropy code; 2.678 bits/exp vs 2.645 entropy (98.8% efficiency), 0.033 bits from exponent-only floor. Kept because the Shannon-gap argument for rANS buys almost nothing on this data.

nodes.label: Entropy codes are not homomorphic
nodes.rationale: A codeword is a frequency-chosen index with no arithmetic relation to its value, so computing on compressed data without decoding is impossible; the homomorphic route is scale-factor representation, i.e. INT8/INT4 quantization, which is lossy. Reachable goal is GEMM fusion, not deleting the decoder.

nodes.label: Field split (exponent coded, sign+mantissa raw)
nodes.rationale: Sign and mantissa entropy is near maximal, so only the exponent is coded. Costs 0.076 bits/weight (0.47 points) vs a full 16-bit alphabet coder by subadditivity; 0.040 of it is I(exp;mant) concentrated in binades 122-123.

nodes.label: Fixed-width quantization formats (GGUF, GPTQ, AWQ, NF4)
nodes.norm_label: fixed-width quantization formats (gguf, gptq, awq, nf4)
nodes.rationale: Production lossy formats avoid entropy codes not because Huffman is slow but because variable-length codes destroy random access and force a decompress-to-memory round trip instead of in-register dequantisation in the GEMM.

nodes.label: Fused BF16 output (merge sign+mantissa in kernel)
nodes.norm_label: fused bf16 output (merge sign+mantissa in kernel)
nodes.rationale: Separate merge pass moves 256 MB, almost 3x the decode kernel; fusing drops pipeline traffic ~345 -> ~217 MB and removes a launch. DFloat11 already does this; needed for Phase 3.

nodes.label: GEMM fusion of decompression
nodes.rationale: The standalone decoder pays a full memory round trip; fusion removes global-memory materialisation and overlaps decode with tensor-core work. This, not rANS, is what gives 2606.15789 its 11x. Plausible next move: keep canonical Huffman and fuse.

nodes.label: Huffman over exponent pairs
nodes.rationale: Halves the serial chain iterations and is 0.0164 bits/symbol smaller, for an 8 KiB LUT. Speculative, not yet tried.

nodes.label: Kraft inequality check
nodes.rationale: A code with Kraft sum > 1 is undecodable even if it appears to work on some tests; every table must satisfy Kraft <= 1.

nodes.label: Ladder prefix code (1,1,1,2)
nodes.rationale: Fixed-shape prefix code with a 10 B table meant to decode faster than Huffman's 4 KiB LUT via clz+branch+shift. Refuted: 0.86 points worse and 5-43% slower on Pascal, Ampere and Ada; one shared-memory LUT lookup beats a dependent clz/branch/shift/mask chain.

nodes.label: Output staging in shared memory (coalesced write)
nodes.norm_label: output staging in shared memory (coalesced write)
nodes.rationale: Each thread writes BLOCK consecutive bytes so a warp's stores hit 32 sectors; staging through shared memory gives 1.92x on Pascal, 2.61x A100, 4.55x 4090. Input staging alone was worth 1.01x.

nodes.label: rANS / interleaved ANS
nodes.rationale: One-register decoder state and interleaved lanes give coalescing in the format; raw rANS is LIFO so has less inherent seekability than Huffman. Case for switching here is weak because Huffman is already at 98.8% efficiency on the exponent alphabet.

nodes.label: Serial chain of dependent loads per block
nodes.norm_label: serial chain of dependent loads per block
nodes.rationale: After access pattern and index are fixed the decoder sits at 10-45% of peak bandwidth and its time tracks SM clock (4090 2.2x faster than A100 with half the bandwidth): bound by the 64-step dependent-load chain, which only fusion or wider-than-one-thread decode can hide.

nodes.label: Early return before __syncthreads is UB
nodes.rationale: Caused non-deterministic incorrect output in the ladder kernel at BLOCK=512/1024; every thread must reach the barrier. Motivates verifying bit-exactness before timing.

nodes.label: Attribution discipline: measure all combinations, re-run rather than extrapolate
nodes.norm_label: attribution discipline: measure all combinations, re-run rather than extrapolate
nodes.rationale: All input x output staging variants compiled separately, which is how 'both worse than output alone' on Pascal became visible; when the bottleneck moves the Huffman-vs-ladder comparison is redone.

nodes.label: Analytic compression accounting
nodes.rationale: Sizes computed exactly from symbol counts: bits/weight = 8 + avg_exp_bits + 8*bytes_per_block/BLOCK; best whole-model config = 10.818 bits/weight = 32.39%. Header excluded, table included.

nodes.label: Correctness protocol: bit-exact before timing
nodes.rationale: Encoder verified byte-for-byte against the reference BitWriter; Kraft checked for every table; verify_kernels.py compares GPU output with np.array_equal on 32M symbols across 20 BLOCK x threads combos; setup scripts abort on failure so a remote operator cannot produce timings from a broken decoder.

nodes.label: Rule: predictions recorded before measurement and kept as written
nodes.norm_label: rule: predictions recorded before measurement and kept as written
nodes.rationale: Every prediction is written in the document describing the measurement before it runs and left in place whether or not it survived, so refuted hypotheses (the ladder, the input-staging threshold) are reported as failures rather than rewritten.

nodes.label: Hierarchical LUT Huffman decoder (11-bit primary table, 4 KiB shared)
nodes.norm_label: hierarchical lut huffman decoder (11-bit primary table, 4 kib shared)
nodes.rationale: Primary table indexed by the next 11 bits (2048 x 2 B) with canonical search for rare longer codes; one shared-memory access per symbol.

nodes.label: Hypothesis: ladder code decodes faster than canonical Huffman for <1 point
nodes.norm_label: hypothesis: ladder code decodes faster than canonical huffman for <1 point
nodes.rationale: Recorded in the first commit with its own most likely failure mode ('a curiosity 0.8% worse than Huffman') and the deciding question of whether the kernel is memory- or compute-bound. Rate half held (0.86 < 1 point); speed half refuted on three architectures.

nodes.label: The 8-bit index is the portable contribution
nodes.norm_label: the 8-bit index is the portable contribution
nodes.rationale: Nothing about the scheme depends on the entropy code; any fixed-symbols-per-block stream with bounded block-length spread can use it. Saves 2.9 B/block vs uint32 and about a third vs DFloat11's gaps.

nodes.label: Claude Code usage and self-audit disclosure
nodes.norm_label: claude code usage and self-audit disclosure
nodes.rationale: Claude Code implemented codecs, kernels and harnesses, drove rented GPU runs and drafted all docs under the author's direction; every commit carries a Co-Authored-By trailer and session link so division of labour is auditable. Pre-publication audit traced every number to its log and found the duplicated tensor and a wrong literature claim.

nodes.label: L2-per-resident-thread sanity check of rented instance
nodes.norm_label: l2-per-resident-thread sanity check of rented instance
nodes.rationale: setup_cloud.sh prints L2 per resident thread; if it reads 50-85 B instead of ~190 B the pod is not the card ordered and should be terminated.

nodes.label: Speed/compression tension dissolved by the 8-bit index
nodes.norm_label: speed/compression tension dissolved by the 8-bit index
nodes.rationale: Before: fastest BLOCK=64 30.14% vs best BLOCK=1024 33.07% but 32x slower; after: BLOCK=64 32.39%, gap 2.93 -> 0.68 points, no choice left to make.

nodes.rationale: lm_head.weight and embed_tokens.weight are bit-identical duplicates and are dropped.

nodes.label: bench_gpu.mem_floor (memory-floor kernel)
nodes.rationale: Reads the same 32-bit words and writes the same bytes as a decoder thread but does no decoding; an empirical ceiling for that access pattern, not the hardware. Fed the ladder stream, so slightly pessimistic for Huffman.

nodes.label: Nsight Compute unavailable (Pascal unsupported, counters blocked in containers)
nodes.norm_label: nsight compute unavailable (pascal unsupported, counters blocked in containers)

nodes.label: Same-hardware replication run (results/gtx1050ti, 2026-09-13)
nodes.rationale: RESULTS.md tables were transcribed from interactive runs whose output was not saved; the committed logs are a full run_all.ps1 replication. Every ratio reproduces, absolute times move 1-6% (unlocked-clock noise floor).

nodes.label: lts__t_sector_hit_rate.pct (L2 hit rate counter)
nodes.rationale: The decisive Nsight Compute column: should collapse between BLOCK=128 and 256 on a card showing the cliff and stay flat on one that does not.

nodes.label: Phase 2: GPU kernels, memory-bound at BLOCK=64
nodes.norm_label: phase 2: gpu kernels, memory-bound at block=64
nodes.rationale: At BLOCK=64 both decoders are within 1-2% of the memory floor (9.70/9.73/9.57 ms) and the ladder is marginally slower; at BLOCK>=128 the ladder wins 5-32% but 3-13x slower absolute. 8.2% of peak: bound by bad access pattern, output is 71% of traffic.

nodes.label: Phase 2e: L2 prediction on A100 and RTX 4090
nodes.norm_label: phase 2e: l2 prediction on a100 and rtx 4090
nodes.rationale: Cliff 16.2x -> 1.96x -> 1.71x (confirmed); input staging 4.4x -> 2.0x -> 1.2x (decays, not switches off); large BLOCK moot (3-6x slower); output+input staging best on Ampere/Ada; optimised time tracks SM clock; ladder/Huffman 1.055 / ~1.0 / 1.3; 8-bit index free.

nodes.label: BLOCK cliff as an L2 effect
nodes.norm_label: block cliff as an l2 effect
nodes.rationale: 16x collapse between BLOCK=128 and 256 on Pascal coincides with the resident working set crossing 1 MiB L2. Predicted before measuring to shrink on large-L2 cards; held as trend (16.2x -> 1.96x -> 1.71x) but corrected as threshold: input staging decays rather than switches off.

nodes.label: L2 per resident thread
nodes.rationale: The governing figure for the cliff is not L2 size but L2 divided by resident threads: 85 B (1050 Ti), 73 B (3060), 190 B (A100), 194 B (H100), 384 B (4090), 534 B (4070). Used to pick which card to rent.

nodes.label: Timing protocol (CUDA events, warm-up, median of 11, shuffled order)
nodes.norm_label: timing protocol (cuda events, warm-up, median of 11, shuffled order)
nodes.rationale: Clocks cannot be locked under WDDM or in rented containers, so the harness compensates with 0.6 s warm-up, 11 reps with median and IQR, fixed-seed shuffled configuration order, SM clock sampling and a clock-invariant SM-cycles-per-symbol figure.

nodes.label: RTX 4070 prediction (Linux operator guide)
nodes.rationale: At 534 B/thread the BLOCK cliff should disappear up to BLOCK=1024 (working set 24.5 MB fits in 36 MB L2). If it collapses the same way the L2 explanation is false. Run has not happened.

nodes.label: RTX 3060 prediction: cliff in the same place despite 3x L2
nodes.norm_label: rtx 3060 prediction: cliff in the same place despite 3x l2
nodes.rationale: At ~73 B/thread the cliff should appear between BLOCK=128 and 256 despite 3x L2, 4.7x SMs and 3.2x bandwidth: working set 3.73 MB vs 3 MB L2. Tests the per-thread rather than absolute-L2 reading on different silicon.

nodes.label: Recommendation: rent A100 80GB
nodes.rationale: Fills the middle of the L2-per-thread range (85 -> 190 -> 384 -> 534) and is DFloat11's target hardware so claims become directly comparable. RTX 4090 is the cheap alternative; 3090/A6000 (~50 B/thread) are worse than the 1050 Ti.

nodes.label: Rented-GPU prediction: cliff flattens, input staging stops helping at BLOCK=256
nodes.norm_label: rented-gpu prediction: cliff flattens, input staging stops helping at block=256
nodes.rationale: Recorded before renting so the result can be read without help; if the cliff is still there the L2 explanation is false and RESULTS 2b must be rewritten. Outcome: cliff prediction held, input-staging prediction failed.

nodes.label: Residual large-BLOCK slowdown = under-occupancy
nodes.rationale: On A100/4090 the remaining 2x at BLOCK=1024 is not L2: the floor kernel rises the same way and only 62,500 threads exist for ~200k resident slots; affects any one-thread-per-block decoder.

nodes.label: Entropy Code or Memory Layout? (BF16 compression report)
nodes.author: Arnau Ferrerons Manich
nodes.norm_label: entropy code or memory layout? (bf16 compression report)
nodes.rationale: Pre-registered test of whether a table-free ladder prefix code decodes BF16 exponents faster than canonical Huffman on GPU; negative result, but led to the 8-bit block index and shared-memory output coalescing.

nodes.label: DFloat11 5-bit per-thread gap index (two-pass decode)
nodes.rationale: Fixed bytes per thread + 5-bit gap, ~0.21 bits/weight, requires a counting pass plus prefix-sum then decode pass.

nodes.label: Field-split rate floor (0.076 bits/weight gap)
nodes.rationale: True floor H(sign,exp,mant)=10.578 bits; field split achieves 10.678; mutual information exp/mant 0.040 bits concentrated in top two binades.

nodes.label: Fused decompression into GEMM
nodes.rationale: Recommended next step: keep canonical Huffman and fuse, since remaining cost is output traffic and serial chain which fusion hides.

nodes.label: L2 cliff at large BLOCK sizes
nodes.norm_label: l2 cliff at large block sizes
nodes.rationale: 16x slowdown at BLOCK=1024 on Pascal attributed to working set exceeding 1 MiB L2; shrinks to 1.96x (A100) and 1.71x (4090), scaling with L2 per resident thread.

nodes.label: Memory-floor kernel
nodes.rationale: Reads/writes exactly the bytes a decoder thread would, without decoding: a ceiling for that access pattern, not the hardware.

nodes.label: Optimised decoder bound by SM clock (serial dependent-load chain)
nodes.norm_label: optimised decoder bound by sm clock (serial dependent-load chain)

nodes.label: RTX 4090 base-kernel benchmark (Huffman vs ladder vs floor)
nodes.norm_label: rtx 4090 base-kernel benchmark (huffman vs ladder vs floor)
nodes.rationale: 64M Qwen3-0.6B symbols; BLOCK 64-1024 x 64-256 threads; Huffman 1.23-2.38 ms, ladder 1.20-2.18 ms; ladder/huff 0.83-0.98; floor 1.22-1.78 ms. Saved to outputs/gpu_bench.json.

nodes.label: RTX 4090 shared-memory staging benchmark (base vs smem in/out)
nodes.norm_label: rtx 4090 shared-memory staging benchmark (base vs smem in/out)
nodes.rationale: Output staging gives up to 5.64x at BLOCK=64 (~0.21 ms, ~419 GB/s); input staging alone ~1.0x at BLOCK=64; configs over 48 KiB shared memory skipped.

nodes.label: RTX 4090 8-bit index benchmark (uint32 vs uint8+prefix-sum)
nodes.rationale: BLOCK=64/128 thr: Huffman 0.19 ms both, compression 30.73% -> 32.97% (+2.25 pts); BLOCK=256 fails (length range 409 > 255).

nodes.norm_label: approaching shannon bound (tan et al., isca 2026) — rans + fused gemm

nodes.label: Canonical Huffman exponent code (11-bit 4 KiB LUT)
nodes.norm_label: canonical huffman exponent code (11-bit 4 kib lut)
nodes.rationale: One shared-memory lookup per symbol beats the ladder's dependent clz/branch/shift/mask chain; 0.033 bits from exponent-entropy floor (98.8% efficiency).

nodes.label: 8-bit block index with warp prefix-sum
nodes.rationale: Block lengths at BLOCK=64 span only 143 bits, so store uint8 length per block plus a uint32 base per 32-block superblock (1.125 B/block vs 4); offsets recovered with five __shfl_up_sync. +2.25 pts compression, zero measurable cost; removes block-size vs index-overhead trade-off. Fails when range >255 (BLOCK>=256).

nodes.label: Ladder prefix code (rungs 1,1,1,2)
nodes.rationale: Fixed-shape prefix code: count leading ones (clz), read rung index into 10-byte table, 12-bit escape. Kraft-complete; only 10 symbol bytes change per model.

nodes.label: Ladder-code speed hypothesis (pre-registered)
nodes.rationale: Hypothesis: a 10-byte-table ladder code decodes faster than 4 KiB-LUT Huffman for <1 pt compression loss. Refuted: ladder loses 0.86 pts and is never faster at the operating point (ratio 1.05/~1.0/1.3 on Pascal/Ampere/Ada).

nodes.label: Shared-memory output coalescing (output staging)
nodes.rationale: Each thread writes BLOCK consecutive bytes so warp stores hit 32 sectors; staging through shared memory coalesces them. Worth 1.92x Pascal, 2.61x A100, 4.55x 4090; input staging alone worth ~nothing at BLOCK=64.
